original_question: Find physically interesting infinite-dimensional billiard systems, ideally arising from equations of mathematical physics such as fluid dynamics or other Euler-Arnold type geodesic equations.
target_in_paper: Boris Khesin, item 1: "Find physically interesting examples of infinite-dimensional billiards." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's intended target: it asks for physically interesting infinite-dimensional billiard systems and explicitly points to fluid dynamics and Euler-Arnold-type geodesic equations, which is exactly how the paper motivates the problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
missing_details: The paper poses an existence/construction problem for examples; it is not a classification statement or a yes/no conjecture about all infinite-dimensional billiards. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The motivating paradigm is that billiard flows should arise as relatives or limits of geodesic flows on infinite-dimensional spaces, with Euler-Arnold equations singled out as a main source of such geodesic equations. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The principal concrete example named is incompressible Euler: solutions are viewed as geodesics on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms with respect to a right-invariant L^2 metric. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The nearby context also names KdV, magnetohydrodynamics, and the Heisenberg chain as further equations/models in the same geodesic-flow spirit; including these keeps the question paper-faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The paper suggests a specific billiard mechanism: not finitely many particles reflecting from a wall, but a continuum of particles doing so. Your draft does not include this concrete modeling direction. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The main obstruction mentioned is that, after reflection, the reflected and pre-reflection motions occupy the same near-boundary region simultaneously, so one must allow a framework with overlapping flows. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The suggested formalism is the multi-phase/generalized-flow setting, specifically via the groupoid structure for generalized flows and boundary conditions in the diffeomorphism groupoid for two-phase fluids, with the broader goal of a theory for multi-phase fluids with billiard reflections from the boundary. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

There are no ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier clauses here; this is a qualitative geometric-analytic open problem rather than an algebraic conjecture with explicit quantifiers. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
refined_question: Can one construct nontrivial physically meaningful infinite-dimensional billiard systems whose free-flight dynamics come from geodesic equations on infinite-dimensional spaces arising in mathematical physics—especially Euler-Arnold equations such as incompressible Euler on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms with its right-invariant L^2 metric, and analogously KdV, magnetohydrodynamics, or the Heisenberg chain—and, in particular, can one formulate a billiard-type reflection theory for a continuum of particles hitting a boundary by using the generalized-flow/diffeomorphism-groupoid framework for two-phase or multi-phase fluids, via suitable boundary conditions that encode billiard reflection? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
justification: The draft clearly targets Boris Khesin's first open problem rather than the Albach-Hryniewicz-Oancea periodic-orbit problems: the paper literally asks for physically interesting infinite-dimensional billiards and motivates this through the billiard/geodesic correspondence, Euler-Arnold geodesic equations on infinite-dimensional groups, and examples from incompressible Euler, KdV, magnetohydrodynamics, and the Heisenberg chain. The paper then makes the scope sharper by suggesting a particular route through continuum-particle reflections, multi-phase flows, generalized flows, and the diffeomorphism groupoid for two-phase fluids. The refined question keeps all of that nearby context and does not broaden beyond the paper's stated intent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
